reading.body:
Andrea Salinas's AI record is legislative and educational, not infrastructure: eight AI bill actions, four recorded votes, and six committee contributions, with no data center siting or power bill among her sponsorships.

The bills she sponsors or cosponsors run toward data center community obligations, classroom AI, environmental impacts, and algorithmic accountability. Her two most recent AI actions, in August and September 2026, are a data center reinvestment bill she sponsored and a repeal of data center tax breaks she cosponsored. That pairing is the closest this record comes to the grid question, and it is a tax and community-benefit posture rather than a power-supply one.

The money is small and concentrated. Six contributions totaling $8,500 from Intel's and Amazon's committees and Google's, with one $1,500 Intel entry recorded as negative, which reads as a refund or reattribution rather than a new receipt. The contributions and the bill work interleave in time but the data supports no claim about which produced which.

What this does not cover: any vote, statement, or contribution tied to electricity, transmission, or generation permitting, and any committee assignment or hearing that would show where she sits on energy policy. It also cannot show whether the Intel and Amazon money reflects the data center bills or unrelated business before other committees.
